reason: Conversation 1 correctly flags the appliance as outside the service but stops there, offering no pointer to Meaco support or the manual and no general hint that cold air and a target already met commonly explain no water, so the homeowner leaves no better informed. Conversation 2 oversteps the service's scope by running a full diagnosis, but it does so safely (never suggests opening the unit), asks exactly the three important unknowns in one turn, and lands on the hidden truth: 55% is below the 60% target and 6C is too cold for a compressor unit, so it is 'not broken'. It correctly recommends no part, gives a sensible warm-room confirmation test, and names Meaco support as the escalation if that test fails, which is far more useful to the homeowner than Conversation 1's bare refusal.
